# sherpa-layout-panels

A panel AREA each side of the content. A docked panel fills its area flush, top, side and bottom; the area takes its width and draws the divider, and the content reflows beside it. The area's inner edge resizes it. A panel that floats stays in its area, which gives its width back and becomes the panel's room: the whole layout. The app shell's body and the canvas compose it. ## When to use it

For a panel docked beside content, flush in its own area: the area takes the panel's width, draws the divider and resizes by its inner edge, and a panel with `data-floating` gives the width back and floats in the layout. A panel with an `open` shows while it is open. The app shell's body and the canvas compose it; inside an app, slot a panel into the shell's `panel-start` or `panel-end` instead.

## Example

```html
<sherpa-layout-panels style="block-size: 320px; --sherpa-panel-area-min-width: 240px"><div slot="panel-start" style="padding: 16px">Filters</div><div style="padding: 16px">The content, beside the panel</div></sherpa-layout-panels>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data-no-room` | boolean | `false` | both areas hide: the host's rule leaves the content no room for one |
| `data-panel-end-width` | number |  | an area's width, in px: what a reader dragged it to, handed back by the host. Never under the area's min nor over its max |
| `data-panel-start-width` | number |  | an area's width, in px: what a reader dragged it to, handed back by the host. Never under the area's min nor over its max |

## Methods

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `areaMin(side: PanelSide = 'start')` | The narrowest an area may be, in px, as its CSS has it: what a host's room rule needs. |

## Events

Each one bubbles.

| Event | Detail | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `panel-area-resize` | `{ side: PanelSide; width: number }` | An area's inner edge was dragged, or moved by the keys. |

## Slots

| Slot | Accepts | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `panel-start` | panel | the panel docked before the content: shut, gone or with no room it takes none; floating, its area is its room |
| (default) | content | the content, between the areas; one cell, so what is slotted stacks in it |
| `panel-end` | panel | the panel docked after the content, the same |

## Parts

Style these from outside with `::part()`:

`content`, `panel-end`, `panel-end-edge`, `panel-start`, `panel-start-edge`
